packages/ble/src/e2e.test.ts.content: The selector is created and asserted (`currentKind()` === "toolkit-ble") but the data path never uses it: `nobleSim.scan(...)` and `new BleLink(..., nobleSim, ...)` bypass `BackendSelector.scan/connect` entirely. So the header claim "selectable by the DS-04 decision switch" and the auto/failover behaviour are not exercised end to end — indeed the only peripheral is registered on `nobleSim`, so a scan through the selected toolkit primary would return zero results. Drive scan/connect through `selector` (or add the peripheral to the primary) to actually verify the decision switch.

The per-frame assertion only checks the link's own counter (`writesSent`), which is incremented before/independently of `connection.write()`. A codec/serialization regression or dropped write would keep this at 80 while nothing reaches the device. Assert the bytes that actually landed (e.g. `peripheral.metrics.writes` and `peripheral.written`/`painted`) so delivery is proven, not just the internal count.

`catch(() => null)` swallows every failure mode into `null`, so the one-connection guarantee passes for the wrong reason (e.g. a wrong address would also resolve the chain to `null`), and it does not confirm the adapter rejected the second connect with the expected error. Assert the rejection explicitly.

`advance` re-scans `this.tasks` and processes any timer whose `at <= target`, so a callback that re-arms a timer at the current instant (a 0 ms delay, which this harness allows via `writeDrainMs: 0`) keeps being selected and the `for (;;)` loop never terminates, hanging the suite instead of failing it. packages/ble/src/stream.ts.content: Quantisation groups by the quantised bucket key but stores the raw first-seen RGB as the group colour, so the emitted masked write carries an *unquantised* colour while all later zones in the same bucket are forced onto that first zone's exact value. The quantised palette is therefore never actually transmitted: e.g. with `quantizeLevels: 4`, `[250,0,0]` and `[255,5,5]` collapse into one bucket and both zones are written as `250,0,0`. If the intent is to snap zones to a representative palette value, store the bucketed colour instead; if the intent really is "first-seen colour wins the bucket", document it explicitly, because the current code contradicts the "quantisation reduces distinct colours" description at the top of the file.

Empty-frame fast path emits a spurious write. When `zoneCount` is 0 (or the frame is otherwise empty) `distinctColours` is 0 and `singleColour` becomes true, so `encodeBleStreamFrame` falls into the fast path with `writes[0]` undefined and synthesises a black `bleColorSingle`/`bleHostColorOne`. That is a whole-fixture colour command (no mask) emitted for a frame with no zones, and it makes `writes` (length 1) disagree with `feedback.distinctColours` (0). Return `[]` for zero zones instead of a fabricated colour write.

const first = plan.writes[0];
    const color: BleRgb = first === undefined ? { r: 0, g: 0, b: 0 } : first.color;

packages/ble/src/stream.ts.content: `budgetHz` is never validated, so a zero/negative/NaN budget silently produces `Infinity`, a negative, or `NaN` in `effectiveFps` (and only the `distinctColours === 0` branch avoids a divide-by-zero). Downstream planner/mixer code that simplifies patterns on `effectiveFps < showRate` will silently never trigger on `NaN` comparisons. Validate `budgetHz` (finite, > 0) at entry, or clamp the result, and surface a clear error for bad planner input rather than emitting misleading feedback.

packages/controller-flx4/src/map.ts.content: The LSB lookup key is built from the unmasked byte (`data1 - 0x20`) while the MSB branch stores under the masked key (`${status & 0xff}:${data1 & 0x7f}`). For any input where the LSB's data1 carries a stray high bit (or is below 0x20) the two keys never match and the 14-bit pair silently stays incomplete forever — no error is surfaced beyond `complete:false`. Mask consistently (and ideally derive the MSB number from the control definition instead of assuming a fixed +0x20 offset). Note also the incomplete branch returns `(data2 & 0x7f) / 16383` (~0) whereas the MSB branch returns `data2/127` (full scale); a consumer that applies `value` without checking `complete` will snap a 14-bit control to minimum.

`raw` masks all three bytes (`& 0xff` / `& 0x7f`) but the switch below consumes the raw, unmasked `data2` and `data1`. `decode()` is a public entry point taking plain `number`s, so an out-of-range byte produces a jog delta / button state that disagrees with the `raw` tuple reported in the same event. Mask once and reuse the masked values in the switch (and mask the `decodeBytes` fallback raw too, which currently emits unmasked bytes).

packages/dj-core/src/index.test.ts.content: The `auto` fallback case asserts only the `fellBack` flag, not the returned `position`/`source`, so a wrong fallback value or a wrong reported source would go unnoticed. More importantly, the suite never covers the case that matters for DS-26: a present-but-stale/zero reading masking a live one. Concrete failure: `resolveCrossfader("auto", { software: 0, controller: 0.9 })` currently returns `position: 0, source: "software"` (0 is treated as a valid finite reading), silently discarding the live controller value, yet every existing assertion still passes. The sharp-cut boundary is only probed from the A side below/at center and B at center. B just below 0.5 (which must be 0) is never asserted. Concrete failure: an implementation of the form `side === "A" ? (p < 0.5 ? 1 : 0) : (p <= 0.5 ? 1 : 0)` keeps both decks audible across the center, yet all three existing sharp-cut assertions still pass. Add the B-side lower-boundary cases.

packages/govee/src/scenes.test.ts.content: The test name claims scene resolution returns *copies*, but `toEqual` only compares values and never mutates the returned array or checks reference identity. A regression where `sceneFromCatalog` returns the catalogue's own array (violating the copy contract at scenes.ts:38) would still pass, silently allowing callers to mutate shared catalogue state. Mutate the result and assert the catalogue is untouched (or assert `not.toBe`).

The round-trip only checks `msg.cmd` and that the encoder decodes back to the same array; it never pins the actual wire field (`msg.data.command`, the byte strings). Because both sides of the assertion go through the same module, a self-consistent but wrong envelope (wrong field name/encoding) would still pass, and this module's whole purpose is matching the govee2mqtt LAN wire shape. Assert the full envelope literal.

The file header asserts scene code resolves for setup/idle/ending moments and never for show frames, but only the `ending` branch is exercised here. The `setup` and `idle` moments are never tested, so a regression that (for example) resolves only for `ending` would pass unnoticed. Add assertions for the other moments (the type `SceneMoment` already excludes "show", so at minimum cover setup and idle).

packages/renderer/src/color.ts.content: `fixtureBytes` re-implements the numeric gamma transfer instead of delegating to `linearToSrgbByte`. Unlike `linearToSrgbByte`, this copy (a) has no `gamma > 0` guard, so a calibration gamma of 0 or negative is used directly (`1/gamma` becomes Infinity or negative), and (b) does not clamp the `pow` result before `Math.round(... * 255)`. For example `gamma = -1, v = 0.5` yields `Math.round(0.5**-1 * 255) = 510`, a byte value outside 0-255, while `linearToSrgbByte` would fall back to `DEFAULT_GAMMA`. It also propagates NaN silently (Math.min/Math.max pass NaN through, Math.round(NaN) => NaN, which a Uint8Array store then truncates to 0). Delegate to `linearToSrgbByte` so both paths share the guard and clamp.

  const transfer = (v: number): number => linearToSrgbByte(v, gamma);
